title: insitro's AI drug-prediction models go live for biotechs on Lilly's TuneLab platform
source_used: BioSpace (insitro press release); Dealroom page was blocked
key_facts: insitro, an AI drug-discovery company led by founder Daphne Koller, announced on 6 Oct 2026 that its machine-learning models built with Eli Lilly can now be used by certain biotech companies in Lilly TuneLab.
The models predict how small-molecule drug candidates behave in the body (in vivo) as well as in lab assays (in vitro).
They were trained on multi-species preclinical data Lilly generated over decades from hundreds of thousands of unique molecules.
The collaboration was announced in September 2025; the models will be updated as the dataset grows.
Koller says nine in 10 programs entering the clinic fail, often because the molecule does not reach the tissue at the right concentration.
insitro says better prediction at the design stage could mean fewer flawed candidates advance and less reliance on animal studies.
quote_evidence: Nine in 10 programs that enter the clinic fail, most often when we first test for efficacy.
These models make it a computational question first.
why_it_matters_hint: Smaller biotechs get access to prediction models built on data only a large drugmaker could generate, which may help screen molecules earlier.
notes: Dealroom page blocked (Cloudflare). Read insitro's own press release as carried by BioSpace. All claims are the company's own; no independent evaluation reported.
